alex: Quick heads-up — ran an apples-to-apples pass (straightedge-1k) comparing dispatch vs eager rotary kernels. Seeing ~7% median/p95 RT regression on eager when KV cache is warm. Anyone else seen this?

marta: Hmm that's larger than I'd expect. Did you pin decode params & stop seqs exactly?

alex: Yep — same seed/prompts, top_p=0.95, temp=0.0, stop=['\\n', '###'], decode length fixed. Tokenizer alignment used tokenizer-v2. Harness was replay-based (no synthetic). Logs + config below.

cheng: Can you paste the exact run command and the perf counters you collected?

alex:
```
./run_apples --harness straightedge-1k --model rdx-open-7b --kernel eager_rotary --decode-params "temp=0,top_p=0.95" --tokenizer tokenizer-v2 --batching dynamic --max-batch 32
```

Perf excerpt (warm KV runs):
```
median latency: 312ms (dispatch)
median latency: 334ms (eager)
p95: 680ms -> 728ms (+7.1%)
GPU util: dispatch 78%  eager 83%
KV hit ratio: 99.2% (both)
kernel launches: dispatch 420k, eager 512k
small-kernel tail (% of launches <200us): dispatch 18% eager 29%
```

simone: Interesting — eager shows more small kernel launches and a higher GPU util. Could be launch overhead + memcpy boundaries around KV reads. Do you have an nsight timeline or nvprof snapshot?

alex: Pasted a short trace snippet: a recurring pattern where a tiny memcpy follows a KV read and precedes a GEMM; wall time stalls ~120-200us on those boundaries repeatedly. Repro >90% across seeds and prompt subsets.

marta: Check batching heuristics — dynamic batching + eager seems risky. We saw cases where dynamic coalescing produced lots of small micro-batches that blow up launch counts for eager kernels. What was dynamic target latency?

alex: target_latency=80ms, max_batch=32. I also tried fixed=16 earlier and the eager vs dispatch gap shrank to ~1-2% (within noise).

cheng: So likely interaction between dynamic batching and kernel launch characteristics. Proposal: (1) re-run fixed-batch apples (16, 32) across both kernels, (2) run a cold->warm KV sweep (cold, 1warm, 10warm repeats), (3) collect kernel call counts + launch latency distribution (hist). I'll drop a tiny collector script.

infra-bot: job 2849123 finished: apples straightedge-1k fixed-batch-16 (success) :white_check_mark:

cheng: Collector snippet:
```
# collect kernel metadata
python tools/collect_kernel_stats.py --run straightedge-1k --out /tmp/ks_straightedge.json
# fields: kernel_name, launch_time_us, bytes_memcpy, stream_id
```

simone: If launch overhead is the culprit we have two levers: enable kernel fusion (experimental) or adjust batching/coalescing (merge small requests into micro-batches). Kernel fusion reduced small-launch tail in our earlier microbench by ~40%. Worth A/B.

alex: Good plan. I'll: run fixed-batch sweep across kernels, run cold->warm KV sweep, and enable fusion flag in a canary. Will attach traces. Running first batch now, will update when complete. Thanks all :thumbsup:
